The company plans to enter the electricity business using this technology. Some predict that every existing power company could disappear as a result.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k191: Omoto Trading's Top Ten Stories, Part 8
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k192:
This series presents last year's ten biggest stories from Omoto Trading, known for its many Asaseo Wharf warehouses and wide-ranging distribution business. Eighth: 100 additional large tankers enter service.

Omoto has added 100 large tankers dedicated to its own distribution network.
Developed in-house, they combine ample cargo capacity with comfortable crew quarters. Skilled sailors from other companies are reportedly transferring in large numbers.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k193: Omoto Trading's Top Ten Stories, Part 9
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k194:
This series presents last year's ten biggest stories from Omoto Trading, known for its many Asaseo Wharf warehouses and wide-ranging distribution business. Ninth: electronic cargo transmission begins.

After years of research, Omoto has finally brought into commercial use a device that electronically transmits packages.
If widely adopted, this revolutionary system could send cargo to the other side of the planet in minutes without transport vehicles.
For now, it requires dedicated lines and carries high usage fees.
The company says ordinary power outlets should support it within two years.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k195: Omoto Trading's Top Ten Stories, Part 10
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k196:
This series presents last year's ten biggest stories from Omoto Trading, known for its many Asaseo Wharf warehouses and wide-ranging distribution business. Tenth: the headquarters cherry tree turns 1,000.

A cherry tree planted by Omoto's founder on the headquarters grounds has reached 1,000 years of age. This also marks the company's thousandth anniversary.
Despite that remarkable history, the president says, "We're aiming for our ten-thousandth."
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k197: The History of Asaseo Wharf, Part 1
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k198:
About 700 years ago, Asaseo Wharf was still sea.
More precisely, it was a gently shelving coast. Written records describe thriving clam gathering there.
This was an age of scattered settlements containing only a few homes each.

It must have been a majestic landscape, almost impossible to imagine amid today's concrete.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k199: The History of Asaseo Wharf, Part 2
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k200:
By about 500 years ago, roughly half the shallows had been reclaimed and a town resembling a post station was developing.
Most travel through the area was still overland.
Several businesses paid specified taxes for exclusive sections of the remaining shallows, where they gathered and sold clams.
Some apparently charged visitors to enjoy recreational clam digging during holiday seasons.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k201: The History of Asaseo Wharf, Part 3
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k202:
Around 300 years ago, all the shallows had been reclaimed and the shore transformed into timber landing stages.
This could be considered the origin of today's wharf.
The change dramatically improved maritime distribution, and surrounding towns reportedly prospered.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k203: The History of Asaseo Wharf, Part 4
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k204:
Around 150 years ago, expanded landing facilities and storage buildings made this one of the country's three largest ports of its kind.
Becoming a major maritime transport hub brought further growth.

Nearby farmland gave way to homes, shops, and lodging.
The community rapidly transformed from an agricultural town into a commercial center.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k205: The History of Asaseo Wharf, Part 5
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k206:
By wartime, the modernized wharf included a shipyard that built several enormous battleships.
Lodging and entertainment facilities served workers gathered from across the regions, and their spending enriched the town further.

After the war, the shipyard closed. New berths and warehouses replaced it, creating roughly the Asaseo Wharf we know today.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k208:
Did you know that modern warehouses are being developed and sold with functions beyond simple storage?
Today's example doubles as a nuclear shelter. It can reportedly withstand ten consecutive direct nuclear missile hits without destruction or contamination. Dedicated filtration and climate control keep the air clean, while Omoto Trading's Ultra Super Solar system supplies power, making it virtually self-sustaining forever.

Unfortunately, you must supply your own food, though its spacious interior could accommodate a vegetable garden.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k210:
Did you know some warehouses can move on caterpillar tracks?
They transport the cargo and the entire building together.

Already used in a country largely overtaken by desert, refrigerated and freezer warehouses crossing the sands like ancient caravans make an impressive sight.
More wharves are also adopting them because they can move out of harm's way during disasters, avoiding secondary damage.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k212:
There are even warehouses that fly using jet propulsion.
Like vertical-takeoff aircraft, they need no runway.
They also run on Omoto Trading's Ultra Super Solar system, eliminating fuel-cost worries.

By making the building itself a transport vehicle, goods can be distributed an entire warehouse at a time.

They also offer an innovative evacuation method during earthquakes and other disasters: simply rise into the unaffected sky. Adoption has begun in public facilities as well as businesses.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k214:
Some warehouses become ships themselves.

With their own propulsion, they can head out to sea carrying their contents without transferring cargo onto a vessel.
Many readers may have seen the recent advertisement in which numerous warehouses arrange themselves into a company logo in the middle of the Pacific. This is that product.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k216:
One warehouse combines every function discussed here.
It serves as a nuclear shelter, travels on tracks, flies by jet, and becomes a ship.
Its price is in a different league, but it is arguably the ultimate warehouse.

Military use might seem tempting, yet the company's peace-loving president apparently enforces a strict prohibition.
Do you remember the country ruled by a tyrant that was reduced to scorched earth overnight about six months ago?
Persistent rumors say its secret purchase of these warehouses for misuse incurred the president's wrath.
Of course, all uninvolved civilians were reportedly moved to other countries first: a splendid gesture.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k217: Seven Mysteries of the Wharf, Part 1
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k218:
Cargo that vanished overnight

Asaseo Wharf's long history contains many strange events.
About 70 years ago, cargo stored in its warehouses disappeared in a single night.
The staff responsible had checked their inventories before going home,
so the warehouses had not been empty to begin with.

Night guards were on patrol, but reportedly saw nobody moving goods.
Even a conservative estimate puts the missing cargo at several hundred tons.
Who could have taken so much, and how, without being noticed?
The truth remains unknown.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k219: Seven Mysteries of the Wharf, Part 2
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k220:
The warehouse district with no exit

Asaseo Wharf is lined with countless warehouses.
It is said that once you enter certain parts, the buildings continue endlessly and you cannot find a way out.
Records describe several workers entering the district and never returning.
Some suggest they simply left by another route and moved away.
Or perhaps they are still wandering among the warehouses.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k221: Seven Mysteries of the Wharf, Part 3
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k222:
Children's laughter on the midnight wharf

From spring into early summer, excited children's voices are said to echo around Asaseo Wharf late at night.
Hearing them brings no particular misfortune, but people find them eerie enough that nighttime patrol wages are higher during that season.

Long ago, this area was a shallow coast popular for clam digging.
Perhaps the joyful voices of children from those days are reaching us across time.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k223: Seven Mysteries of the Wharf, Part 4
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k224:
The mysterious Mr. Yamazaki

Workers at Asaseo Wharf are familiar with an employee called Mr. Yamazaki.
Yet he belongs to none of the companies operating there, and may not even be human.

Although he appears to be in his early forties, accounts of him date back more than 200 years.

Knowledgeable about many things, he casually appears whenever someone is in trouble and offers sound advice. The wharf's workers reportedly welcome him.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k225: Seven Mysteries of the Wharf, Part 5
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k226:
The calico cat that never leaves

A calico cat has lived at Asaseo Wharf for as long as anyone can remember.
Its distinctive back markings suggest the same cat has been there for around 100 years.

Usually unseen, it occasionally appears, sits with its paws tucked beneath it for a while, then wanders away.
What matters is where it sits: the next day, misfortune invariably strikes a person or company associated with that spot.

The day after it was seen sunning itself on a gantry crane, the crane collapsed into a nearby tanker, causing a major fire.
On another occasion it lay down inside a warehouse. The next day, the owning company's headquarters burned down in a suspicious fire.

Wharf workers believe the cat does not bring bad luck, but comes to warn them.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k227: Seven Mysteries of the Wharf, Part 6
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k228:
The unreachable corner

An area of Asaseo Wharf is said to be impossible to reach, no matter how one tries.
Maps show an ordinary warehouse, but every route fails to lead there.

Someone reportedly tried photographing it from above. The images clearly showed the warehouse exactly where the map placed it.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k229: Seven Mysteries of the Wharf, Part 7
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k230:
The statue that patrols at midnight

Asaseo Wharf once had a bronze statue of an elderly man.
It honored local notable Tokuzo Yano, whose generous donations and tireless efforts to attract businesses helped modernize the wharf.

Some say they saw his statue patrolling the grounds late at night.
Perhaps his lifelong love for this wharf lingered within the bronze.

The statue is now kept in the city museum. To honor his achievements, the city intends to preserve it carefully and seek national-treasure status.
So far, nobody has reported it patrolling the museum.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k231: What Can You Find at the Wharf? Part 1
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k232:
At a wharf, you often see something shaped like an enormous giraffe.
It is called a gantry crane.

Wharf workers use these cranes to load containers onto ships and lift them off again.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k233: What Can You Find at the Wharf? Part 2
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k234:
Asaseo Wharf has lots of warehouses.
They hold cargo brought by large ships, or goods waiting to go aboard the next one.

There are different kinds. Some keep things cool like your refrigerator at home, while others freeze them solid like a freezer.
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k235: What Can You Find at the Wharf? Part 3
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k236:
The colorful boxes piled high at Asaseo Wharf are called containers.

All sorts of cargo goes inside them to travel on large ships.
It is just like putting your toys in a box to carry them!
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k237: What Can You Find at the Wharf? Part 4
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k238:
Where ships dock, you will see rows of objects shaped like thick, bent fingers. These are called mooring bollards.
Ships are tied to them with very thick ropes so they cannot drift away.

Their shapes and sizes differ between ports and wharves. Have a look when you visit with your parents.
Just be very careful not to fall into the sea!
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k239: What Can You Find at the Wharf? Part 5
common/lua/stage_207_news_text.luc.0:k240:
Looking out from the wharf, you can see triangular objects bobbing on the water.
These are called lighted buoys, and they mark the way so ships do not get lost.

They shine at night, even though there are no power outlets nearby.
How do they make electricity? By bobbing up and down on the waves!

Small models are also sold, so try one and see for yourself.

common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k129: Two more giants: An enormous nuisance
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k130:
Two more giant creatures appeared near Hinageshidai Station.

Apparently hostile to one another, they exchanged threats and occasionally fired beams from their mouths.
Their enormous weight caved in roads with every step, shattering nearby windows and cracking walls. Their tails and beams also destroyed or severely damaged numerous buildings.

Why they chose a city for their confrontation remains unknown. From our perspective, they should have done it on some deserted island or remote stretch of ocean.
If they were deliberately attacking humanity, this would be a battle. Yet they show no obvious interest in targeting people: it seems to be a quarrel between two creatures, making them a nuisance. Given the scale of the damage, we must protest loudly: an enormous nuisance!
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k132:
A creature has appeared that would not look out of place in the dinosaur books of our childhood.
Perhaps it could be described as a stocky, two-legged reptile. Structures resembling dorsal fins sometimes glow, but many terrestrial organisms emit light. What truly distinguishes it is its enormous size and the beam from its mouth.
That beam has extraordinary power, leaving buildings it strikes in a pitiful state.

Could this creature descend from dinosaurs thought extinct? Analysis of the footage is underway, and we will report further findings.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k134:
An enormous golden body, three necks and heads, and wings: what should we call this creature?

It looks like a monster from mythology. Many say myths are merely stories, while others argue they arose from something real. Is it too wild to suggest that this creature has existed somewhere on Earth since ancient times, simply escaping discovery?

Humanity boasts of its progress, yet new species are still found every day.
Our civilization has certainly advanced, but it has not become all-knowing or all-powerful.

I will never forget watching it fly away and feeling something more divine than frightening.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k136:
"Trains were running and people needed somewhere to escape. Closing the station never crossed my mind," Hinageshidai's stationmaster told a press conference.

A giant creature's long, thick tail lay directly in front of the entrance. As its owner fought another giant nearby, the station kept its shutters open and continued operating.

When the stationmaster finished speaking, the room erupted in applause, a rare sight at a press conference.
True crises test human dignity, and this seemed a perfect example.

Still, am I overthinking things to wonder why the stationmaster was sweating quite so unnaturally heavily?
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k138:
Curiosity can make people gather at fires, fights, and crime scenes despite the risks.
But seeing a young person filming giant creatures on a phone while clearly in mortal danger seemed a step too far.

He was neither a journalist risking his life to report the truth nor someone physically capable of withstanding a giant creature.
His awareness of danger was plainly inadequate. Whether he was among them is unknown, but 21 people are believed to have died while similarly absorbed in filming this incident. All were in their early twenties.

It may be premature to generalize about youth, but statistics also show declining risk awareness year after year. That is deeply concerning.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k140:
The overpass on Shirotsumekusa Street, affectionately called the Hand-in-Hand Overpass, has been destroyed.
The golden giant is thought responsible, and damage is reportedly beyond repair.

Its history reaches back to when a river, rather than a street, ran through the town. Settlements on its north and south banks were bitterly divided.
A girl from the northern community fell in love with a man from the south. Their relationship was thwarted, and the two threw themselves into the river.
Her father, leader of the northern settlement, was filled with remorse. He went alone to negotiate with the south, offering his own life in exchange for peace and persuading both sides to end their quarrel.
Around then, plans began to fill in the river. To preserve easy passage between north and south, he spent his fortune building this overpass.

After seeing it completed, he took his own life despite those who tried to stop him.
Moved by his resolve, the communities strengthened their ties, and the crossing became known as the Hand-in-Hand Overpass that united them.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k142:
As people hurried away from the mysterious giants, two motorcycle riders were seen behaving differently from everyone else.
They appeared to be traveling in the opposite direction.
"Disaster looters" crossed my mind, and I instinctively took a photograph. Sadly, many people exploit such confusion to commit crimes without hesitation.
I am not saying these two were doing so. But having witnessed such situations repeatedly, I found their behavior too troubling to ignore.

Who are these young people, and what are they trying to do? I will continue investigating.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k144:
Not a soul appears in this modern district of office buildings. It looks like a ghost town.
But have you noticed the astonishing detail hidden in the photograph?

Even as two giants rampaged nearby, many people were still working inside.
Look at the numerous lit windows. At first I assumed occupants had fled without turning off the lights, but closer inspection revealed moving figures.

An employee of nearby Company A told me in an impromptu interview, "I know it's dangerous, but my boss and most of my colleagues haven't left..." Is this diligence and loyalty, or the national tendency to conform? We welcome your views.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k146:
A motorcycle stolen from Sky Garden Bridge was found on a road near Hinageshidai Station.

It was in pieces, and investigators are considering deliberate vandalism.
Giant creatures were also seen nearby, and police say they are actively investigating whether those caused the damage.

Owner Shizuo Sato, a pseudonym, looked despondent during an interview. "I still have two years left on the loan..."
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k148:
Little-known toothpick manufacturer Johma's headquarters was half-destroyed by a giant creature's tail.
Half remains standing, but the building is unusable.

It housed "Toothpicks: Everything," an exhibition of toothpicks from every era and region, and the Tsumayo Theater, where toothpick idol Tsumayo-J performed daily. The building was a pilgrimage site for a reported ten million fans in Japan and two billion worldwide.

With operations halted, most precious exhibits lost, and the theater gone, condolences and encouragement are arriving from across the globe.
A fan-led appeal has already raised over four billion yen. The mecca's return may not be far away.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k150:
The strange beams fired from the golden monster's three mouths matched the color of its body.
Despite their horrific destructive force, many witnesses described the gleaming light as almost divine.
Humanity has revered gold and its color since ancient times. Is that because it symbolizes the sun?
Today, gold also represents wealth. Images of the beams are reportedly spreading online as phone wallpapers believed to bring financial luck. Should we condemn such a lack of caution, or admire the resilience?
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k152:
Collapsed buildings and destroyed roads were found throughout the area where two dinosaur-like giants appeared.
This photograph shows one junction: a major intersection gouged out, with surrounding asphalt peeled upward into walls.
Utilities beneath the road have naturally been severed too. Repairs will require enormous expense as well as time.
Nearby offices are unusable, inflicting huge losses on their companies.
Some are seeking temporary premises, while many others cannot afford even that and have no option but bankruptcy.
The scars left by these giants are deeper and wider than this photograph alone can show.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k154:
We captured an astonishing scene when the golden creature's beam caused a tanker truck to explode.
The white car in the air was thrown by the blast. Can you see a motorcycle lying sideways beneath it?
It has not simply fallen: it is sliding on its side beneath the airborne car.
I had seen this in films, but never expected to witness it myself.
After avoiding the car, the rider smoothly righted the motorcycle and slipped past the burning tanker as though nothing had happened.
The rider appeared young. A professional, perhaps, or a miracle born of crisis?
Either way, it was proof that such a feat can happen without camera tricks or computer graphics.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k155: What drives riders beneath a monster?
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k156:
We captured two motorcycles racing around the feet of a creature whose single foot could block two or three lanes.
Were the riders on some vital mission, or simply acting without thought?
For a moment I even wondered if they had a death wish, yet they skillfully slipped through.
The motorcycles have been identified as those seen behaving suspiciously in several locations.
Perhaps these young people are not human at all, but human-looking beings controlling the giants.
Following them might reveal why the creatures appeared, and perhaps how to repel them.
Our investigation continues. Watch for updates.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k158:
This crushed, burned-out car was parked immediately behind a tanker when a giant creature's beam made the tanker explode.
Owner Shigehisa Kano, 28, a pseudonym, had come to collect his girlfriend on their first anniversary.
He parked outside the building containing her private office. Inside, she was with another man and accused Kano of stalking her. The man had connections to the Metropolitan Police, and Kano was immediately taken to a nearby station.
Police ignored his protests. He was finally released only after signing a pledge not to approach her again.
Bewildered and exhausted, he returned to find his ruined car dozens of meters from where he had left it.
"...Did I do something wrong...?" he murmured. I could find no words to offer.

Some witnesses later told us she had remarked, "I don't think I can squeeze any more money out of him. Time to find someone new."
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k159: An unlikely benefit of fallen plants?
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k160:
We received some information that is hard to believe.
If you looked at the pictured plant and wondered why nobody had stood it back up, so did I.
It was not knocked over by an earthquake or accident. It was laid down deliberately.
Research claims that plants on their sides produce ten times the normal amount of the relaxing substance "shinotony," and the practice is slowly spreading through offices.
Users report striking results: "It looked odd and we doubted it, but business performance rose 10%," and, "People look calmer, and communication is smoother."
The institute behind the study says, "We found that plants, like humans, relax more when lying down, stimulating shinotony production." I have already begun trying it in our office and will report the results next time.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k162:
Here is an update on the Yukiyanagi Building, a few minutes' walk from Hinageshidai Station, which we have covered several times.
As previously reported, its many young IT firms give it a bright, fresh image that appeals to young people.
Yet more suspicious activity has come to light. When two mysterious giants confronted one another directly outside, several people were seen entering and leaving the building.
They were not fleeing danger: they deliberately passed beneath the creatures to enter, then emerged some time later.
We have also learned that one carried a suspicious box.
Some suggest they were retrieving important documents or looting, but I disagree.
I already know that several tenants have business partners that cannot be clearly identified.
We will continue investigating.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k164:
This time we visit Hinageshidai Station.
Now used by more than 100,000 passengers a day, it began as a peaceful stop surrounded by fields.
Few know it was not originally planned at all. A local major landowner's word led to its hurried addition.
Its unusual location beneath the elevated tracks, rather than in a separate building alongside them, was a desperate measure to open with the railway.
Buying adjacent farmland would have been straightforward, but there was not enough construction time, resulting in today's arrangement.
The decision was decidedly self-serving, yet nobody could have foreseen the rapid urbanization that would turn it into a major station.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k165: Companies We'd Like to Work For, Part 11
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k166:
Our eleventh installment introduces Design Office Kezurokka.
This group specializes in advertising and web design. Some staff also program and compose music, allowing complete project packages that keep major corporate orders coming.
Every employee, including the president, is a woman. Childcare and home-working arrangements are extensive.
Only two years after founding, the current office is already too small, and a company building is under construction.
The priority, however, is not rapid mass recruitment. It is creating an easier working environment with an on-site nursery, medical facilities, a supermarket, and other shopping services.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k167: The station kiosk's light and shadow
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k168:
I spoke with a woman who kept her station kiosk open as usual while giant creatures rampaged nearby.
"It seems we're the only shop still open..." Something caught in her voice, so I pressed gently.
Her answer was dispiriting. "Management told us not to close. They said it'd make a heartwarming story and raise the share price." She continued, "They said they'd fire me if I shut, blacklist me, and make sure I never worked again. Of course my life matters, so I'll run if I have to."
Having spoken, she smiled as though relieved. "Now I've said it, I'll be fired. But I feel better. Write it up. It's the truth."
This article may cost her job. As its author, I want to help her too. Using the USB drive she handed me before we parted, I plan to expose the company's darker side next time.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k170:
Top of the station's seven mysteries would have to be Hinageshidai Station's restrooms.
Whatever the time, they are always closed for cleaning.
Both the men's and women's facilities are unavailable.
The operator insists, "Inspection reports say they are functioning normally."
Station staff give evasive answers, so I rather insistently accompanied one to see for myself.
A man in a cleaner's uniform stood at the entrance and said cleaning was underway. I stubbornly waited two hours, but it never finished. Asked again, he said a broken water pipe meant closure for the day. Every visit during a full week followed this pattern; I never managed to use them.
Later, I saw the supposed cleaner working in the staff office in a station uniform.
Why does the station persistently deny access while maintaining the appearance that the facilities are normally open?
And why does the operator insist nothing is wrong? Questions abound.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k172:
Today we meet Tatsuya Konoe, 28, of much-discussed Hinageshidai Station.
Interviewer: "How long have you been a station employee?"
Konoe: "A little over a year."
Interviewer: "What did you do before that?"
Konoe: "I started an internet company at university and continued running it after graduation."
Interviewer: "Did things go wrong?"
Konoe: "No, sales kept growing steadily."
Interviewer: "Then why become a station employee? A childhood dream?"
Konoe: "I'd earned more than I could spend even if I played until I was 100, so I got bored. I wrote a simple program to select a job at random. It picked station employee, so I used a connection to get hired."
Interviewer: "So you have no particular attachment to the work?"
Konoe: "You could say I'm attached to how entertaining it is. Seeing people desperately commute on tiny salaries and allowances is rather amusing, even while I pity them."

Continued next time.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k174:
Surprising information has emerged about Katsuko Mitarai, 38, a relief activist frequently seen on television defending vulnerable people's rights and living conditions.
This photograph, taken inside Hinageshidai Station, clearly shows her demanding something of an employee.
She was insisting that the station shutters be closed, even though two giants had appeared nearby and many people outside were still trying to escape. According to the member of the public who took the photograph, she petulantly demanded closure to protect herself. She apparently justified it as helping those already inside, but objectively seemed concerned only with her own safety.
They say crises reveal our true selves. Is this the real Mitarai?
Am I alone in finding her activism suddenly less convincing?
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k176:
People were still working furiously in a building beside the giant creatures.
As a giant struck the building, windows shattered, walls cracked, and papers scattered everywhere, they continued calmly. The scene was at once awe-inspiring and horrifying.
When I tried visiting later, the building was closed because of the risk of collapse.
Management could not be reached, and we still do not know whether the workers escaped.
I can only pray I imagined the faint tapping of keyboards carried down from the upper floors on the wind.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k178:
Office desks have reached a new stage of evolution.
Meet Jobu, the multifunction desk made from the extremely hard material Ekipotan. It can reportedly withstand an impact of up to one million tons.
Hiding beneath it will protect you even if the ceiling falls.
It also offers shelter from the bomb attacks that have recently become more frequent.

There is one drawback: it weighs a ton. Strong buildings should cope, but users in aging premises should beware of it falling through the floor.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k180:
Today we introduce Mamoru from the popular multifunction-desk series.
It transforms into protective clothing covering the entire body.
Though weaker than Jobu, it reportedly offers durability comparable to a conventional bulletproof vest.
Even its drawer becomes a helmet, providing head-to-toe coverage.

It is reassuring when a disaster forces you through dangerous areas.
However, transformation is complicated, so we strongly recommend practicing beforehand.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k182:
Good news for companies that frequently move desks as their teams change.
The Karukaru multifunction desk is made from the special fiber Tetofanu. Its hollow body weighs just 100 grams. A standard built-in computer precisely manages internal air pressure, so neither resting hands nor heavy objects make it deform like a balloon.
It can also be deflated, allowing an entire desk to be carried in a shirt pocket.

Such lightness might sound unstable, but suction beneath the legs anchors it even to carpet, making it feel like a normal desk.

Just be aware of the electricity bill.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k184:
The Sui multifunction desk answers the wish, "Wouldn't it be convenient if the whole desk could glide around?"
At the touch of a switch, spherical rollers emerge from its legs. Connect the chair using the supplied parts, and it moves effortlessly.
Deliberately avoiding motorized movement also helps combat inactivity, and the desk boasts strong weight-loss results.

Power outlets are included. Plug the supplied charger into an office outlet and it wirelessly powers the desk's contactless battery, letting a computer keep running as you move.

Unfortunately, the system is so powerful that it also draws electricity from chargers in neighboring offices.
Some users deliberately install none of their own, effectively stealing power.
An identification feature would seem to solve this, but for some reason the design remains unchanged.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k186:
An office reportedly received a strange late-night fax.
Written as though with a finger dipped in liquid, it said, "B E H I N D."
Another arrived at the same time the next day. The message was identical, but the handwriting differed slightly, as though freshly written.
The faxes continued for two weeks.
Police would not take the matter seriously, so the staff hired a detective to trace the sender.
The number was quickly identified, but it had been unused for decades, and its former owner was dead. The detective located the owner's former home, now vacant.

No connection could be found between the office staff and the deceased or any relatives.
The faxes continued daily throughout the investigation, even after the office changed numbers.
When the same message still arrived with the machine unplugged, a human explanation seemed impossible.

Who was sending them, how, and why?
"I've solved it. Th..." The detective's telephone report broke off there. The detective then disappeared.
Several others were hired, but all vanished just as they seemed to reach the answer. The rumors have now made it impossible to find anyone willing to investigate.

The fax still arrives at the same time every day.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k188:
Shelves packed with neatly filed documents are familiar to office workers, especially those in white-collar jobs.
Despite computers becoming ubiquitous and decades of talk about going paperless, the sight persists.

Even signatures can now be supplied on pen tablets. Why can we not move beyond paper?
One theory links it to the desire for possession: the reassurance of holding a physical object rather than electronic data.
For generations not born into a world of computers, unfamiliar digitization can feel unsettling, while paper can be seen and touched.

Some paper records deserve preservation for emotional reasons too.
Yet I cannot help feeling that much of what we keep is unnecessary.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k190:
Office cabinets are familiar, but this model contains some remarkable new equipment.
Its coat compartment becomes an emergency refuge capsule.
Step inside and press the rear switch to lower a shutter, sealing you away from the outside.
It is waterproof. Devices concealed in the frame filter outside air and supply it within; remarkably, they can even generate air when the cabinet is surrounded by seawater.
A portable toilet and ventilation prevent odors building up.
A monitor displays nearby conditions using exterior cameras and sensors as well as high-resolution images from a dedicated satellite.
Satellite monitoring also means a specialized rescue team can respond immediately if the cabinet is trapped beneath rubble or underwater.

It is astonishing how far technology has come.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k192:
Water dispensers promise clean drinking water whenever you need it and are widely used in offices and homes.
But is that water really safe?
A supplier was exposed last week, though a political scandal overshadowed the news. It had been selling tap water in tanks labeled "pure water."
It also added disinfectant calcium hypochlorite as a precaution, followed by the compound Monefrio to conceal the smell.

Worse, it collected worn-out tanks discarded by competitors and reused them without permission.

The tap water itself was taken late at night from parks and other public facilities. Words fail us.

Can you trust your dispenser supplier?
We recommend checking the Consumer Affairs Agency website's list of companies whose safety has been verified.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k194:
Everyone knows the red button above a fire-hose cabinet sounds an emergency alarm.
Yet how many people feel tempted to press it just by looking? Doing so without an emergency is nothing but a nuisance. Even adults who know better can feel the urge.
Research reportedly links this to stress. The more stressed someone is, the more tempting it becomes: doing something forbidden, or watching others panic, might offer relief.
An urban legend offers another explanation: the button supposedly emits waves that attract attention and curiosity.
This seems too implausible to take seriously, and dismantling units has revealed no such device. Manufacturers naturally deny it too.
Still, something troubles me. During a factory visit, I briefly glimpsed what looked like an altar inside the warehouse of finished units. The door closed immediately, and my escort's face seemed to tense for a moment.
I will continue investigating. Watch for updates.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k195: Untidiness can be a serious problem
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k196:
A mountain of cardboard boxes blocks this office corridor.
They contain documents and other materials with nowhere else to go.
Such a sight is deeply disappointing, because it sharply reduces the occupants' chances of surviving a disaster.

I have investigated numerous cases where piled documents blocked emergency stairs, or collapsing boxes trapped and killed people.

You need not tidy merely for appearances. Do it to help yourself survive.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k197: A device meant to save lives...
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k198:
A malicious incident involving an AED has come to light.
A young person used one on an elderly man who collapsed with breathing difficulties, but sadly he could not be saved.
An ordinary person using an AED in an emergency is not criminally responsible simply because the rescue fails.
So what was wrong?
It was a premeditated crime.
The young person had targeted a wealthy stranger, beginning with apparently chance greetings in the park until the old man trusted them like a grandchild.
With no family, the man believed the lies, adopted the young person, and arranged a large insurance payout in the event of his death.
The culprit also gradually weakened him by adding a drug to tea and other drinks.
That led to his collapse in the street.
Terrifyingly, the AED's use was apparently manipulated as well.

The circumstances initially prompted no special investigation, and the scheme seemed successful.
How was it exposed?
The truth is revealed in Miracle Mysteries: Modern Sentiments, on sale now.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k200:
Did you know an ordinary station ticket machine has a unique hidden trick?
Press particular buttons in a particular sequence and rhythm, and a special ticket appears.

It cannot be used for travel, but handing it to a station employee gets you something in exchange.

Unfortunately, we cannot reveal the precise method or the reward here.
I did obtain the special ticket, however, and what I received enriched my life considerably.
Anyone fortunate enough to get one is sure to find happiness.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k201: Cash hidden in school fire cabinets
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k202:
The day after the giant-creature commotion subsided, an incident unfolded at an elementary school near Hinageshidai Station.
A rescue worker surveying damage found bundles of banknotes scattered along a corridor. Apparently the previous day's shocks had opened a fire-hose cabinet, spilling the cash hidden inside.
The principal arrived moments later and admitted concealing it.
He had tried reaching the school during the crisis, but blocked roads delayed him until morning.
More bundles were found in other fire cabinets.
They were accumulated payments for recommendations securing admission to prestigious middle schools.
Usually kept in his home safe, the money had been hurriedly moved to school after he learned of a pending investigation. The giants appeared that very day.
Crime does not pay. Police intend to identify the people who made the payments as well.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k204:
Have you heard the rumor that Hinageshidai Station's coin lockers connect to a secret underground facility?
Open certain lockers in a particular order and speak specified words before one, and a passage supposedly appears behind them, leading below.
It is said to shelter selected dignitaries in an emergency.

The station operator politely denied its existence and even showed us plans.

But I saw it. During the giant-creature crisis, prefectural assembly member Kamozo Gokita disappeared behind the lockers. When I approached, there was indeed a passage wide enough for one person.
I tried entering, but a man in black suddenly appeared. Sensing danger, I fled.

As I type this, I can hear someone trying to enter our office.
If I escape, I intend to continue investigating and report the truth.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k205: The secret of the trash cans
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k206:
Hinageshidai Station has equipment that looks ordinary but is actually cutting-edge.
Its trash cans are one example.
They automatically shred and digest their contents. "Digest" may not be technically accurate, but in any case, garbage left inside eventually disappears.

If you have the chance, watch one for a while. You should see the contents gradually diminish before your eyes.

The devices are reportedly research prototypes installed here to collect data.
Naturally, they also have extensive anti-theft protection.
The project is revolutionary and apparently involves the government. If successful, it could help eliminate the world's mountains of waste.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k208:
Did you know the door to Hinageshidai Station's staff room was made by Shunya, third son of the master Shunzo Sanuki?
It was the first door he created as a beginner. Unlike his father, a designer capable of almost anything, Shunya is acclaimed as a sculptural artist. Though currently focused on sculpture, he excels in other fields too, and many hope he will eventually follow his father's broader path.

Before finding his artistic direction, he made this door while helping his father. It is now valued at 300 million yen.
Its rarity accounts for that price: it remains his only architectural work.

Perhaps the apple truly does not fall far from the tree.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k210:
A man was seen photographing the giant creatures at extremely close range.
He climbed onto an abandoned car and shot intently while an enormous tail passed directly above.

He turned out to be a freelance photographer, but even professional duty seems a questionable reason to take such risks.
When I reached him later, I put that concern to him.
"There are things only I can do. That's all." With those words, he left for his next assignment.
The resolve of photographers and journalists may be stronger than I imagine.
Still, sometimes avoiding danger is necessary too.
Lose your life, and everything else is lost with it.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k212:
A woman stood dazed near Hinageshidai Station's ticket gates, surrounded by scattered cans of juice.
She had visited shop after shop amid the giant creatures' rampage before finally finding them. Then a young person rushing into the station collided with her, spilling every can and its contents onto the floor.

She lived alone with her young child, who was in bed with a fever.
The child wanted a currently popular juice, so she had wandered the night streets despite the giants. At last she found some near the station and bought the entire remaining stock. She was heading home when the collision ruined everything.

It is hard to blame the young person, who was surely desperate to escape the obvious danger.
The mother said she felt no blame either. But she added, "I don't know how to face my child," and, "I can't go home like this." Then she walked back into the city where the giants still raged.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k214:
A man fidgets endlessly outside a public restroom marked "Cleaning in progress."
Many people know the experience: you rarely need it, but just when you urgently do, it is being cleaned.
"Why now?" you think. With another restroom too far away to risk, you decide cleaning cannot take long and keep waiting.
Statistics suggest this often ends with a search for another restroom anyway.
Cleaning takes more time and effort than people assume.
It may therefore be wiser to start looking elsewhere as soon as you see the sign.
Apps now show nearby available public restrooms, and we recommend using one.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k216:
They all look almost expressionless.
They neither flatter customers nor take the superior attitude of "I'll buy it if you're desperate."
They remain composed at all times.
Details were not disclosed, but company training apparently instills this mindset.
The staff look so alike, in more than just clothing, that an urban legend calls them clones. That too seems to be the result of training.
Yet their hidden passion is clear in their eyes. They shine with the thought, "Making customers happy by buying their goods is our joy."
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k218:
This time, the Elevator Appreciation Society visited the Yukiyanagi Building.
Its elevator is not a standard manufacturer's model, but a special design by the great Shunzo Sanuki.
Already retired, he created this exceptional piece because the building's owner was a close friend.

As readers know, Sanuki never compromises. Workers reportedly had to redo the installation repeatedly. Yet his remarkable influence did not end there: those same workers' skills improved dramatically afterward. They are now leading specialists and technical advisers at major construction firms, all saying, "Studying under Sanuki then was where everything began."
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k220:
Our popular Tipsy Tours series, written on the momentum of a pleasant buzz, reaches installment 10482.

Today we examine emergency stairs.
When slightly drunk, resting a cheek on a step feels wonderfully cool.
They are also ideal for quietly crouching when feeling low.
Outdoor stairs without enclosing walls can even serve as a kitchen for grilling dried fish during late-night overtime.

Be aware that, especially overseas, security arrangements may prevent stairwell doors above the ground floor from opening from inside.
Do not accidentally enter a high-rise stairwell and find yourself forced to descend an absurd number of floors.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k221: The sound of typing late at night
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k222:
Late at night, keyboard tapping echoes through a dim office.
A man works alone.
He founded the company and now runs it by himself. As usual, he is typing relentlessly to meet a deadline the next morning.
This situation is apparently almost constant. He seldom returns to his apartment, bathing and washing clothes at nearby facilities.
He says he enjoys his work. But should such conditions simply be accepted?
I know many envy the chance to do work they love for as long as they like. Still, I cannot help questioning whether this is healthy for a living creature, a human being.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k224:
This photograph captures people rushing into Hinageshidai Station while the giants' beams occasionally strike the ground.

Later interviews revealed that they had missed their chance to flee, sheltered in their offices for a while, then finally gathered the courage to run.

Humans often see themselves as rulers of the entire ecosystem, but such scenes reveal that belief's limits. Not only giant creatures, but all kinds of natural disasters leave us powerless.
Our choices are to flee or hide and protect ourselves.
Perhaps this crisis should prompt humanity to reconsider its proper place.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k225: A strange figure in the nighttime office
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k226:
A woman crouched in a dim office.
When approached, she muttered something and shuffled away without standing.
It seemed impossible demands at work had finally made her stress overflow.
Other employees were nearby, but none tried to calm or comfort her. Everyone appeared too overwhelmed.

It should have been a deeply sad scene.
Later, by chance, I learned that she was a troublesome employee who crouched in protest over minor matters.
Forgetting reports or abandoning assigned tasks because she did not know how to proceed were everyday occurrences. When corrected, she behaved this way.
I was astonished by the resemblance to a small child throwing a tantrum in a toy shop.

More disturbingly, such behavior among working adults is reportedly increasing rapidly.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k227: Unaware of danger, or remarkably calm?
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k228:
At Hinageshidai Station, a man calmly played games on his mobile phone.
With giants rampaging nearby and others terrified or fleeing, his ordinary composure held my attention.

Curious, I spoke with him. He reasoned very logically and clearly understood the danger.
His ability to remain so calm despite that knowledge impressed me greatly.
I asked about his occupation, but he only gave a slight smile and declined to answer.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k229: "Where can we go?" People flee in confusion
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k230:
Few people recognize the danger of getting out of a stopped car to inspect a sudden incident.
On highways and ordinary roads alike, other cars and motorcycles may still be moving. Standing carelessly in the roadway risks being struck from behind.

It is understandable to panic in a situation one never expected to face.
Precisely then, however, everyday habits of caution can help prevent another accident.

Many realize this only once involved themselves. I hope this article can offer a useful lesson to as many readers as possible.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k231: Buildings fall as crowds search for safety
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k232:
People flee to avoid debris from collapsing buildings.
As in earthquakes and other disasters, staying somewhere less exposed to collapse is important.
On a broad avenue, one example is the central divider, which also reduces the danger from vehicles approaching behind.

Recognizing that many ordinary objects can become hazards, and mentally rehearsing such situations beforehand, is essential.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k234:
One woman remained inside the station rather than fleeing the crisis.
She was waiting for her boyfriend of about three years.
She could not reach him, had lost one of the earrings he gave her on their first date,
and had also dropped the matching watch they bought together.
Despite these ominous setbacks, she simply waited.
Perhaps unwilling to show her devotion, she affected irritation and complained about his shortcomings.
But she kept waiting bravely while trembling with fear.
The expression that flashed across her face when he finally arrived said more than anything else.
She quickly hid it, scolded him, and left the danger zone at his side.

Amid so much grim news, I am grateful to the couple for this heartwarming sight.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k236:
The changing staircase

The Yukiyanagi Building has a staircase whose number of steps changes.
The emergency stairs connecting the third and fourth floors reportedly have twelve steps at times and eleven at others.
This is not merely rumor: recorded measurements exist.

Like many readers, I was skeptical and investigated in person.
I confirmed that it really happens.

It is neither illusion nor trick. The same staircase changes its step count.
When there are fewer steps, each becomes slightly taller and deeper, so the flight remains continuous.

The mechanism is unknown, but statistics suggest the timing is related to the tides.
We will report further findings as they emerge.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k238:
The mysterious floor

Like some other buildings, Yukiyanagi has no floor labeled four.
The physical fourth floor is called the fifth,
and the elevator has no fourth-floor button.

Yet occasional reports claim such a button has appeared.
Those who reported it were too frightened to press it.

There are also accounts of one worker vanishing suddenly every five years.
Perhaps each simply left a tenant company without saying anything.
Still, the possibility that they pressed the fourth-floor button cannot be ruled out.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k240:
The rooftop shrine

A shrine stands on the Yukiyanagi Building's roof.
Long ago, the site was home to a merchant.

His commercial skill won business with samurai households and lords, but that success led to tragedy.

A powerful lord took an interest in his daughter.
He forcibly carried her to his mansion, then had the merchant and his wife killed in what appeared to be a bandit attack to conceal the crime.

Believing he could now do as he pleased, the lord approached the room where she was confined. Suddenly, the supposedly dead merchant stood before him, covered in blood.
Unfazed by several retainers cutting at him, the merchant bit into the lord's throat and killed him.

Pierced by swords and spears, with hands and a leg torn away, he still found his daughter and carried her home in triumph.
Only upon reaching home did he collapse.
It is said that love for his daughter and sheer determination moved his body even after death.

The daughter later became a nun. People moved by her father's devotion built a shrine on the abandoned home's site.
Over the years, attempts to remove it were followed by mysterious deaths. Thus, even after the office building rose, the shrine remained, now on its roof.

A figure believed to be the merchant is still occasionally seen in its offices.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k242:
The unexplained voices

A story circulates in the Yukiyanagi Building.
Work alone late at night, and the voices of many people can supposedly be heard from nowhere.

It happens on any floor, provided only one person remains there.
The voices stop when the listener looks around, then resume when work begins again. No injury or misfortune follows, but it is unsettling nonetheless.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k244:
The wandering shadow

For years, numerous witnesses have reported something like a shadow crossing the Yukiyanagi Building's corridors.
Security cameras finally captured it, lending truth to the rumors. A researcher has reportedly volunteered to investigate.

Early theories suggested the bitterness of an employee who died from overwork, or the merchant described in Part 3 who once lived here. It now appears to be neither.

No misfortune has been reported by witnesses, yet an unidentified presence remains deeply unsettling.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k246:
The glowing floor

Did you know part of the third-floor corridor in the Yukiyanagi Building glows once every few years?
Several floor tiles light up, and stepping on them changes their colors.

One story says stepping on them in the correct order brings good fortune.
The only employee said to have found that order, about fifteen years ago, reportedly won first prize in the lottery repeatedly and is now extremely wealthy.
However, that fortunate person's identity has never been confirmed, so the truth remains uncertain.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k248:
Writing on the windows

Something resembling letters reportedly appears at irregular intervals on the Yukiyanagi Building's sixth-floor windows.
It cannot be seen from inside, only from outdoors.

The windows have not been altered and are cleaned regularly, leaving the cause unknown.
The writing looks like cursive script, but nobody has deciphered it, so its message is equally mysterious.

Is the building itself trying to communicate with the outside world? We will report the truth if it emerges.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k249: Toro also spotted near Hinageshidai Station
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k250:
Toro, familiar from Doko Demo Issyo, has reportedly been seen near Hinageshidai Station.
Witnesses say he appeared troubled.
Whether he was bewildered by the crisis like everyone else, or had another concern, is unclear.
It is even possible that he was involved in the incident and worried because things had not gone as planned.

There were also reports of Toro exchanging something with a young person inside a vehicle abandoned in the road.
I intend to identify that person and uncover the truth.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k251: The Tale of the Last Sword reaches every UN nation
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k252:
The Tale of the Last Sword, beloved across national and cultural boundaries, is now sold in every United Nations member state. Its famous phrase, "Honerarino Funarama," will be read around the globe.
Professional translators and passionate fans volunteered in every language, allowing its epic, moving story to reach hearts across linguistic barriers.
Most national leaders also love the books, and many approached the author or publisher asking for sales in their own countries. That support likely helped make this achievement possible.
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k254:
Miyato software company Hyacinth Soft is going bankrupt. Its performance had deteriorated rapidly in recent years, and its former manager disappeared. A new representative had recently taken over and sought to rebuild the company, but bankruptcy has now been decided.
Representative Asano said, "I hoped we could make steady progress, even through small jobs, but we couldn't transform our financial position. It's deeply disappointing."
common/lua/stage_208_news_text.luc.0:k256:
A smartphone app developed by Miyato software company Hyacinth Soft is drawing attention.
It teaches arithmetic, mathematics, and baking through a game-like experience. Representative Asano says, "I heard baking requires precise quantities and knowledge of chemical reactions. That sparked the idea: wouldn't learning the two together be fun?"
The recently released beta, a trial version still in development, has been warmly received. Users praise it with comments such as, "Now I understand the Pythagorean theorem," and, "I successfully made cream puffs for the first time!"

common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k60: Late tonight, a mysterious giant lifted a train that had departed Hinageshidai Station on Miyato Electric Railway's Tozai Line.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k61: Passengers evacuate stopped train on foot
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k62: Late tonight, a train that had departed Tsutsujisawa Station on Miyato Electric Railway's Tozai Line stopped because of the giants' battle. Passengers walked along the elevated track toward Hinageshidai Station.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k64: After a mysterious giant lifted a train departing Hinageshidai Station on Miyato Electric Railway's Tozai Line late tonight, the giant of light reportedly took it back and set it down safely.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k66: Local witnesses say the giant of light's entire body turned blue during tonight's battle. The mysterious opposing giant was also confirmed to have changed into a form with wing-like structures at the same time.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k67: Two giants clash above the city
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k68: The two giants that appeared late tonight took to the air but continued fighting above the city. Brilliant sparks flew when they collided. A resident who happened to see them said, "I thought it was a fireworks display."
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k69: Two stoned by passengers: Assault inquiry?
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k70: Police announced suspicions that people stranded on the railway bridge after the train-lifting incident threw stones at two fellow passengers, accusing them of attracting the mysterious giant. The incident came to light when a passenger who did not participate contacted police. However, both victims are missing, as are most alleged attackers after the bridge collapsed, leaving the truth unresolved.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k72:
Destruction of the Hanamomo River railway bridge is expected to suspend Miyato Electric Railway's Tozai Line between Hinageshidai and Tsutsujisawa stations for several months.
Company president Tetsuro Densha told reporters, "We will do everything possible to restore service as soon as we can."
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k73: Giant of light performs graceful backflip
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k74: The giant of light performed a graceful backflip during tonight's confrontation, perhaps to gain distance from its opponent. Some believe it deliberately flipped over the railway bridge to avoid damaging it, prompting suggestions that it bears no hostility toward humanity.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k76:
Passengers on the platform at Tsutsujisawa Station on Miyato Electric Railway's Tozai Line angrily protested to staff after a delayed announcement that the last train had been canceled.
Through the company's public-relations office, president Tetsuro Densha said, "We will do everything possible to make future announcements without delay."
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k78:
Two giants were seen flying low near the Hanamomo River railway bridge on Miyato Electric Railway's Tozai Line.
They reportedly skimmed the elevated tracks while skillfully avoiding buildings.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k80:
A Miyato Electric Railway Tozai Line driver stopped service to protect passengers after becoming caught in the giants' battle. According to passengers, fierce complaints then drove the driver to lie sulking on the track.
President Tetsuro Densha told reporters, "Abandoning passenger evacuation to lie down and sulk on the tracks is unacceptable. We will do everything possible to prevent a recurrence immediately."
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k81: Students release young sweetfish into river
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k82: Local middle-school students released young sweetfish into the Hanamomo River on the 29th of last month. The annual event began twelve years ago. Hanamomo Middle School student-council president Seto, 14, smiled during our interview: "We experienced life's strength up close. I look forward to seeing the fish fully grown." Seto is due to leave for a year of language study in the United States on the 15th of this month.
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k83: A miracle: Saved by a dirty floor?
common/lua/stage_209_news_text.luc.0:k84:
Security guard Kei Biin, 58, was safely rescued moments ago from a building partly damaged by a flying giant's collision.
Biin had been patrolling the top floor alone and was apparently the building's only occupant.
"A stubborn stain on the office floor saved me," he said.
Known for his love of cleanliness, he was removing dirt found during his rounds when the wall ahead suddenly collapsed. Fortunately unharmed, he is now providing police with a detailed statement.

common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k121: Flying monster nest burns; what becomes of Miyato Sky Tower?
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k122:
A giant monster suddenly appeared near Miyato Sky Tower and attacked it with fireballs.
The tower had become a Gyaos nest.

The attack set the nest ablaze, apparently catching most of the Gyaos inside.
Much of Miyato Sky Tower also collapsed.
There is little hope for the people carried there by the creatures.

The giant repeatedly fired indiscriminately at fleeing Gyaos and appears to have wiped them out.
Its fireballs also caused extensive damage nearby.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k123: Giant monster: Humanity's friend or foe?
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k124:
The giant monster that destroyed Miyato Sky Tower appears to have been targeting the Gyaos nest.

Gyaos had swarmed Suzuran Boulevard, leaving many people injured or missing.
Some experts believe the giant monster is the same one seen at Umegaya Intersection.

The incident has prompted comments such as:
"If it was targeting monsters that attacked people, perhaps it's friendly toward us?"

Others disagree:
"It destroyed Miyato Sky Tower and damaged the surrounding area. Even if it drove the flying monsters away, that cannot be forgiven."

Debate over whether the giant is humanity's enemy or ally looks set to continue.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k125: Government had chosen to protect Gyaos!
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k126:
Gyaos, the flying monsters that devastated Suzuran Boulevard, had already been discovered by the government. Authorities reportedly intended to protect them as precious surviving specimens.

The creatures, which partly destroyed Miyato Sky Tower to build a nest, were found to be larger than humans immediately after hatching and to grow at an abnormal rate.
Experts say Gyaos can lay eggs and reproduce without a mate.

The government ultimately failed to respond quickly enough to their explosive growth, costing many lives.

Online criticism of the authorities is widespread.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k127: Tower collapse disrupts some radio stations
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k128:
The collapse of Miyato Sky Tower is expected to affect some radio broadcasts.

Most television and radio stations had moved transmission equipment to the completed new tower, retaining Miyato Sky Tower as a backup, so their broadcasts are unaffected.
A few radio stations had not relocated, however, and are now off the air.
No restoration timetable is available.

Stations currently off the air:
- FM Urashimaso
- Sakura FM
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k129: Gyaos slices up its own tower?
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k130:
A strange sight was reported at Miyato Sky Tower, now a Gyaos nest.
One creature fired a beam at the stairs leading directly to the observation deck, slicing them apart.

Why risk bringing down the entire tower and nest?
An expert suggested, "It may have been destroying escape routes to stop its food getting away."

Human-eating Gyaos possess both formidable reproductive ability and intelligence.
An urgent response is needed, yet the government remains slow to act.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k132:
Further reports confirm that eggs were found in the Gyaos nest.
Experts say a creature can lay viable eggs without a mate.
It sounds unbelievable, but if true, it is terrifying: even a single survivor could begin a new population.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k134:
New information confirms that some Gyaos emit a beam from their mouths. It reportedly slices through anything it strikes.

The government describes it as an ultrasonic attack and has named it the "Ultrasonic Scalpel."
The Japan Medical Association has protested that the term duplicates the name of a surgical instrument.

Whether only certain individuals or all Gyaos can use it remains unclear. Either way, the threat has undeniably grown.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k136:
As more is learned about Gyaos biology, a horrifying fact has emerged.
The creatures were cannibalizing one another in their nest.
Experts suspect they may be able to reproduce and increase their numbers even without an outside food supply.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k138:
How much do you know about Children's Day?
Its constitutional definition is given as follows:

"Respect children's individuality, promote their happiness, and give thanks to mothers."

Yes, Children's Day is also a day to thank mothers.
Why not express gratitude to your parents on Children's Day as well as Mother's Day?
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k139: Government's Dark Secret: News Helicopters in Disguise?
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k140:
After Gyaos nested in Miyato Sky Tower, news helicopters circled nearby.
My independent investigation found that these were actually government aircraft disguised as news helicopters, intended to contain Gyaos within the nest.
Why the disguise? I suspect the government was trying to protect the creatures despite knowing they ate humans.
I intend to continue investigating these suspicions.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k142:
A news helicopter covering Miyato Sky Tower crashed after a Gyaos attack.
Witnesses say it was approaching the tower when struck.
If so, might it have been trying to rescue people abducted to the nest?
The pilot reportedly had no permission to approach the tower.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k144:
After Miyato Sky Tower's upper observation level was destroyed, a female shop assistant reportedly continued serving those stranded on the lower level.

Despite vicious Gyaos nearby, she put sales before her own evacuation.
"As long as even one customer wants to buy something, I cannot leave," she said.
She had been hired at the tower a year earlier. A few months before that, as graduation approached, hundreds of job applications had failed. Then her parents died unexpectedly and a suspicious fire destroyed her home.
Although neither she nor her parents were at fault, she felt responsible to neighbors whose homes also burned. She sold the remaining land and gave them all the proceeds.

With nothing left but the clothes she wore, she sat alone in a park at dusk, stunned.
There were no tears. Too much misfortune had left her unable to feel anything.

An elderly passerby happened to speak to her, bringing light back into her life.
He was the founder and chairman of the company operating Miyato Sky Tower.

After hearing her story, he arranged housing that day and hired her as a shop assistant.
He said he sympathized because he too had lost his parents young and endured hardship.

Since then, she had worked with single-minded dedication,
cherishing the happiness of being alive and able to imagine a future.
Perhaps that history explains her deep care for others and determination to keep serving even in this crisis.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k146:
While Gyaos circled above, this scene unfolded on Miyato Sky Tower's lower observation level.
A dying man and an injured woman huddled together. Their subsequent fate is unknown.
Am I alone in finding it troubling that the woman's ring was later discovered on that same floor?
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k148:
This is material regurgitated by Gyaos.
Someone who escaped Miyato Sky Tower's lower observation level says a person was seen reaching into it.
Why they did so remains unknown.
Were they searching for something, enjoying the texture, or simply overwhelmed by events?

A company interested in its viscosity has reportedly developed a shock-absorbing material using similar components. We will report more when details become available.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k149: The case for AED installation subsidies
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k150:
AEDs are now visible in many facilities.
Their owners or management companies install them, bearing purchase and maintenance costs themselves.
That burden gradually mounts. A set like the one pictured costs roughly 300,000 yen. Batteries last around four years, and the unit's warranty is five, requiring periodic replacement or repurchase. Batteries are not designed for recharging and are generally discarded after use.

AEDs save lives in emergencies and should be available in more places. Yet leaving everything to private goodwill feels wrong.
This is where government should lead. No tax increase is needed: simply reducing unusually high bureaucratic salaries to private-sector levels could provide 500,000 sets. Population density matters, of course, but even a layperson can see the benefit if more than 100,000 units could be allocated to each of the 47 prefectures.

Does government want to protect its people, or its own bureaucrats? That is the question.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k152:
A fire-hose cabinet on Miyato Sky Tower's observation deck was found with no sign of use.
As there had been no fire, that is hardly surprising.

Some nevertheless argue that high-pressure water could have been used against Gyaos to improve survival chances.
I am skeptical. I have heard an urban-legend-like story of such a hose bringing down a helicopter, though not a Gyaos. But these creatures are unknown.
The attempt might equally have angered them and increased casualties.

Self-appointed commentators excel at finding faults and criticizing, yet lack any direct sense of the conditions on the ground. As a fellow member of the media, I can only regret their prevalence.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k154:
Renowned biologist Dr. Yasuke Komada was confirmed to have been on Miyato Sky Tower's observation deck.
Studying Gyaos regurgitation, he realized the creatures expel indigestible material. He says he wants to research samples after escaping.

His extraordinary willingness to act has uncovered many biological secrets.
He became famous after entering a living whale through its mouth and spending three days studying its interior, based in the stomach.
He took care to protect the whale's health, and it was observed living normally after he emerged.
Academia initially dismissed him. Later, his research inside the whale led to a medicine that completely cured human cancer in 98% of cases, earning worldwide praise. The subsequent spectacle of leading academics visiting his home to apologize was widely reported.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k156:
Miyato Sky Tower worker Kosuke Esaka, a pseudonym, witnessed a colleague being eaten by Gyaos.
He barely escaped, but the psychological shock has left him unable to resume ordinary life, and he remains hospitalized.

The colleague was his fiancee's brother, whom he had known for about five years. People described the two as close as brothers themselves.

With their wedding scheduled for next month, Esaka's fiancee is enduring the tragedy while devotedly caring for him.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k158:
Have you heard the persistent rumor that the right-hand elevator at Miyato Sky Tower brings happiness?
One person supposedly confessed love inside and later married. Another, having lost everything when a company failed, found a lottery ticket there. Nobody claimed it, and it won one billion yen.

Tracing the stories reveals something suspicious.
They apparently began with a tower employee seeking to attract customers.
Some subsequent riders seem to have exaggerated their own good fortune, spreading the tale.
I do not dismiss mysterious powers entirely, but perhaps it is the tower, rather than its passengers, that becomes happy. Attendance has more than tripled since the rumor began.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k160:
Miyato Sky Tower's left-hand elevator is known as the high-stakes elevator.
If one or two people ride down, a spirit supposedly always appears, leaving them psychologically damaged by the time they reach the bottom.
The effects are severe, and returning to ordinary life is reportedly rare.
Yet about one person in fifty meets a peaceful-looking spirit and goes on to a prosperous life.
Among people I interviewed, some gained wealth and leisure. Another suddenly developed an extraordinary palate, revived an abandoned dream of becoming a chef, and now works at a leading overseas restaurant.

Because almost everyone suffers devastating harm, the elevator was once closed or staffed to ensure at least three riders descended together.
However, many remained drawn by the promise of a secure future. It now permits one or two passengers if they sign a document accepting responsibility.

Why only on descent? Why no more than two? Why have authorities not intervened? Questions remain. There is even information that the current prime minister rode it before becoming famous. We will report further developments.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k162:
A familiar buyback dealer was spotted quietly standing on Miyato Sky Tower's lower observation level, now part of a Gyaos nest.

Whether people approached despite the circumstances or because of them is unclear, but transactions were reportedly taking place.
ATMs may well fail in such a crisis; there might not even be electricity. Were customers raising money for food and water, or paying for priority escape? We do not know.

The dealer's survival has not been confirmed.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k164:
Miyato Sky Tower was designed by the master Shunzo Sanuki.
His attention to detail extends even to the observation deck's men's restroom.
Astonishingly, he handmade every toilet, establishing a dedicated kiln and personally blending the clay and glazes.
Their exceptional quality prompted requests from other facilities, but he rejected them: "These toilets are ideally suited to this men's restroom and nowhere else." They remain unique to the tower.
When their appraised value reached two billion yen, management tried to prohibit their use, enraging Sanuki. The details are unclear, but normal use ultimately continued.

Dedicated staff now monitor the room and carefully polish the toilets whenever no visitors are present.

With Sanuki deceased and no records of his clay or glaze formulas surviving, their value has risen further, reportedly to six billion yen.

These extraordinarily expensive toilets escaped damage in the incident. I dearly hope we can sit on them again one day.
common/lua/stage_210_2_news_text.luc.0:k166:
The toilets in Miyato Sky Tower's women's restroom were made by Sayoko, wife of the master Shunzo Sanuki.
Every bit his equal in skill, she created these as her only paired project with him, adding to their rarity.
(He made the toilets in the men's restroom.)
They appear almost identical to his, yet reportedly use entirely different clay, glazes, and firing methods.
His later interview remark, "Sayoko is the one person I can't beat," made major headlines.
